subject: RE: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization + migration plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings integration: quick recap + next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Great conversation this morning
- thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before a technical deep-dive: 

Recap of what you shared:
- Current vendor: VectorCloud (exported index available)
- Embedding vector dim: 768
- Index size: ~4M docs (~4M vectors)
- Query load: ~25-40 QPS peak, mostly short queries with occasional bulk searches
- Use case: semantic search + similarity-based recommendations; plan to add a reranker for top results

Redwood high-level recommendation (first pass):
- Vector dimension: consider moving to 1536 for improved recall (we can run an A/B on a sample set). 1536 gives better representational capacity for your corpus size; we can also support 1024 if you prefer a middle-ground.
- Normalization: store L2-normalized vectors and use cosine similarity by default (significant simplification for cross-provider runs).
- Batching: recommend server-side dynamic batching; suggest client batching at 64-128 vectors per request for bulk re-embedding jobs, and allow real-time queries to be single-vector.
- Migration approach: phased dual-write, rebuild index in background, and cutover with canary tests (detailed plan below).

Quick technical notes / asks for the deep-dive:
1) Can you share a small sample export (5k docs) in JSONL format with fields: id, text, metadata? We referenced acme-vector-export.jsonl in attachments as an example format.
2) Any constraints on re-embedding window (e.g., can you do a weekend full re-index or must be rolling)?
3) Security: do you require VPC/private connectivity or can we use standard TLS with IP restrictions and short-lived service tokens?

Attached: redwood-embeddings-specs.pdf (high-level dimensions & normalization options) and a draft mutual-action-plan (MAP) to capture milestones. I cc'd Dev and Soojin to own the technical deep-dive.

Proposed next steps:
- You share sample export and confirm migration window (action: Acme)
- Schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive with Dev + Soojin (action: Redwood)
- We provide preliminary cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) and an estimated effort for phased migration (action: Redwood)

If that looks right I can schedule the technical call for next week
- available Wed/Thu afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap
- this is very helpful. Quick answers inline: 

- We can share a 5k sample export in JSONL by EOD tomorrow. We'll include id, text, title, created_at and a small metadata blob.
- Re-embedding window: prefer a phased migration. We can't do a single weekend full re-index for our production search; need rolling migration over 2-3 weeks.
- Security: we prefer short-lived service account tokens with IP allowlists + support for customer-managed keys (KMS). VPC peering is a maybe
- we need to understand cost and ops overhead.

Also
- current embedding dims are 768 so there will be cost implications if we move to 1536; we want a preliminary cost delta per 1M tokens/vectors. Can you include that in the estimate?

Tom and I are ok with Wed afternoon PT next week for the technical call. Can you put the invite on calendar?

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Engineering Manager, Search | Acme Corp
Sarah.Li@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:30:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Embeddings integration: quick recap + next steps

Thanks Sarah
- great, appreciate the constraints. Below are concrete technical details we'll cover in the deep-dive and the phased migration pattern we propose.

1) Migration pattern (phased):
- Phase 0: dry-run on sample export (5k) to compare similarity/recall between 768 -> existing VectorCloud and Redwood 1536 embeddings.
- Phase 1: dual-write new content to both VectorCloud and Redwood (writes flow to both systems). For historical data, background job to re-embed in batches.
- Phase 2: partial cutover: run queries against both indexes and do A/B evaluation (we can run cosine similarity + reranker cross-encoder for top-50 re-rank).
- Phase 3: full cutover once canary metrics (precision@10, latency, cost) meet your SLOs.

2) Embedding dimensions & normalization:
- Recommendation: 1536 + L2 normalization stored at index time; query vectors L2-normalized before cosine similarity. This keeps cross-provider comparisons consistent. If cost is a blocker we can evaluate 1024 as an intermediate.

3) Batching & throughput:
- Bulk re-embed job: we recommend client batching 64-128 vectors per request; Redwood server runtime will auto-batch incoming requests and can support internal batches up to 256 for GPU throughput. For your ~4M vectors we estimate throughput profiles in the MAP.

4) Reranking approach:
- Use vector search for top-K (K=50 recommended), then run a cross-encoder reranker on top-50 for better precision on the final results. This reduces cross-encoder compute while preserving quality.

5) SDK & auth snippets (example):
- Python: pip install redwood-sdk
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
  embeddings = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-1536", input=[...], normalize=True)

- Auth: support for short-lived service tokens (recommended), API keys with IP restriction, and enterprise KMS integration for customer-managed keys.

6) Routing & structured output:
- We can route requests by region (us/eu/apac) and by SLA tier. For metadata extraction/structured output we support tool-calling patterns (structured json output + function/tool calling hooks) to extract normalized metadata during ingest.

I've attached the MAP with milestones and a first-pass cost delta for 768 -> 1536 (hosted vs dedicated). We'll refine this after we see the sample.

I'll schedule the technical deep-dive for Wed 2026-09-02 1:00pm PT and send a calendar invite. Please let me know if that time doesn't work.

Thanks,
Marissa
